80829.subject: 🪦 Claude broke Github
80829.body:
The Atlas

Автор: GenAI Works


Автор: GenAI Works

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn

Welcome back! Seven engineers replaced source control in five months, Google shipped a model and a place to point it, and Anthropic’s co-founder pulled his self-improvement timeline forward a year.  In today's Atlas Newsletter: Claude wrote so much code that Anthropic dumped git: 2,500 merges a day in May, over 30,000 by September, and 600 PB of daily traffic git was never built for. Google gave you a better model and somewhere to point it: Gemini 4 Argon reaches everyone on Pro, and you can now run your own app on your own phone. Anthropic’s co-founder just moved his timeline up a year: A benchmark where Opus 5.5 beats former OpenAI and DeepMind researchers at designing experiments, for 1/30 the cost. Build cross-app AI agents with a single MCP: One connection, runtime discovery, and no wiring GitHub, Slack and Notion upfront. PS: Want to collaborate with the biggest GTM engine and distribution moat for AI companies? You can feature your tool with us and reach millions. Claude wrote so much code that Anthropic dumped git In May, Anthropic merged about 2,500 code changes a day.  By September it was over 30,000. Claude writing the code caused the jump, and the company doesn’t expect it to slow, because every bottleneck it removes produces more code. Git couldn’t keep up. The main branch history is nearly 100 GB. CI performs around 25 million checkouts a day, which naively fetched over 600 PB of git traffic daily.  At peak they ran several hundred internal git mirrors to absorb it. Git assumes clients work offline with a full copy of the repo. Almost none of Anthropic’s clients are people. They’re agents and jobs that are online by definition. So seven engineers built a replacement called Scion and moved the entire monorepo off git in five months, while daily merge volume rose 10x around them. 200x less CPU and memory than the git mirror fleet Checkouts in seconds instead of minutes CI recovered 25% of its CPU capacity They had handwritten the git-to-Scion ingestion pipeline and thought it was good.  Then they handed it to Claude Mythos Preview and asked for a rewrite.  With no further instructions it came back using 20x less memory and running 4x faster, with every invariant intact. Every engineer on the team now rates Claude a better coder than themselves.  Their job became supplying system-level design judgment and, very often, telling Claude no. Old assumptions broke

80826.subject: Why Taking Smart Risks Can Create Career Stability
80826.body:
Forbes Edge

Автор: Forbes


Автор: Forbes

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/why-taking-smart-risks-can-create-career-stability-forbes-magazine-gdahc?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BnEpmWG%2BiRRO%2F43Qc4uhSVg%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=3sSSuDCOTtKss1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mv86jnya~xy-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mv86jnya-xy
  
If you’re worried about stability in your career, you’re not alone. Across generations, 53% of people define success as reliable work, according to MyPerfectResume. And Millennials and Gen Z prioritize stability above career progression, based on a survey from Deloitte. It may seem wise to avoid making waves in the workplace, but ironically, you can create stability by taking three smart risks in your career right now. Invite New Challenges. One of the primary ways to create security is to step up and take initiative. Employers value people who seize opportunities and take on new challenges. And when your organization values you, they will want to retain and develop you. Speak Up More. You can also increase stability by speaking up and articulating your point of view. We value people who are both confident and competent, and organizations are prioritizing those who have strong communication skills. By taking a clear perspective, you build your credibility and your value within the organization. Network Boldly. You can also build stability by ensuring you have plenty of people who support your career journey. Be bold and ask influential leaders to connect. Ask them for input, advice or mentoring. It may feel risky, but most people appreciate the opportunity to coach others. With a powerful network you’ll have more contacts to rely on as your career inevitably evolves.   The most stable career is built with the currency of credibility. By taking these smart and assertive steps, you can ensure success as things change. — Tracy Brower, Senior Contributor WORK SMARTER  Practical insights and advice from Forbes staff and contributors to help you succeed in your job, accelerate your career and lead smarter.
